newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia studies making paper from palm waste.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia studies making paper from palm waste.

text.p: Malaysia, the world's largest producer of palm oil, is studying the viability of making pulp, paper and other products from oil palm waste, the national Bernama news agency reported on Sunday.

Researchers from University Pertanian Malaysia, Forest Reasearch Institute Malaysia and Palm Oil Research Institute Malaysia have been put together for the project, the agency quoted Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik as saying.
Lim said Malaysia produced 30 million tonnes of oil palm biomass or waste, made up of trunks, fronds and empty fruit bunches, annually, and the country could profit from this.

"If they (the researchers) can come up with a cost-effective project, we do not need to plant any tree for producing pulp and paper in the country, since 2.5 million hectares of land in Malaysia is already planted with oil palm," Lim said.
